summary.name: Web application
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article explaining web applications: application software built with web technologies that runs in a web browser, with its history, multi-tier structure, security concerns and development frameworks.
use_cases: learning how web applications are structured
background on single-page and progressive web apps
history of Ajax and browser-based software
summary.what_it_does: The article defines web applications as software built with web technologies that runs through a web browser, contrasting them with static web pages. It describes the common three-tier structure (browser presentation, application engine such as PHP or Node.js, and database storage) and mentions n-tier and two-tier alternatives. It gives a historical timeline from the 1999 Java Servlet specification and Ajax to the 2015 coining of "progressive web apps". It also outlines security concerns such as authentication, authorization and input handling, and notes that web application frameworks speed up development.
notable: Covers the three-tier (presentation, application, storage) architecture and n-tier variants
Traces history from Java Servlet 2.2 (1999) and Ajax to progressive web apps (2015)
Discusses security practices for web apps and browser tab sandboxing
caveats: Article is flagged as having multiple issues and some sections need more citations
Describes a concept rather than a downloadable tool or product
